evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: So we talked to a lot of people everyday and most of them have one or two concerns either the movers are not showing up on time or damage to their items, or either of those concern for you.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Rep acknowledges both concerns (on-time and damage), reflects them back, but does not probe deeper with follow-up questions like 'tell me more about that' or silence to allow customer to expand.
evidence_quotes.value_days: No mention of Value Days, day-of-week pricing, or flexibility around the chosen date to save money. Rep offers Monday-Tuesday-Wednesday-Friday-Saturday availability but never circles back to identify which days are cheaper or whether customer can shift dates for savings.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Rep states 'there's no deposit required, no risk in securing your spot' and 'Would you like me to lock that in for you?' — but this is phrased as an ask for the booking before the rate lock is explicitly promised. The rate-lock commitment should come first, then the ask. The no-deposit part is mentioned, but as part of explaining the risk-free nature, not as a lead-in to the ask itself.

top_strength: Zhang delivered both promises (On-Time Guarantee with specific dollar amounts and No Worries Damage Coverage up to $2,000 with no deductible) with clear, recognizable language and all pricing framing components (contrast to hourly competitors, no-notes line, fee transparency, 15-minute increment billing, not-a-guess commitment).
coaching_note: Step 2 needs deeper follow-up: when the customer names a concern, ask 'tell me more about that' and hold silence instead of moving immediately to reflection. Also, Step 6 asks for concerns but misses the catch-all question ('Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'), and Step 7 should lead with rate lock and no deposit as the persuasive frame before asking for the booking.
